title: NEW PROJECT? REUSE SKYFORGE'S SCHEDULING TEMPLATE
headline: ONE ENGINE · ONE SOURCE-CONTRACT · INDEPENDENT PROJECT RECORDS
memory_cue: Open the A7 source pointer, copy the Skyforge template, preserve the project's original text in Drive, derive one WBS/schedule through the shared engine, then validate Gantt/Calendar/Resources before release.
project_adoption_prompt: Continue work on PROJECT_NAME / PROJECT_ID using the current verified Skyforge Standard Project Schedule Template; do not create or fork another scheduling engine.

Read the Skyforge v1.16 tagged architecture, the source JSON template and schema; check the present kernel branch for newer compatible source contracts. Read A7 governance and the project's source register before making any changes.

Verify the project's own identity and Google Drive original documents. For Nepali input, keep an immutable Nepali transcription and a separate traceable English working translation, and derive from English only after comparison to the original. Preserve exact units, dates, constraints and source lines.

Create a separate project-specific source edition from the reusable template; maintain source IDs and WBS/activity IDs, relative-vs-dated calendar basis, working-day vs elapsed-day lags, crew availability, quantities/units, references, holds and unresolved assumptions. Never copy project quantities or engineer decisions from Narayani or Harisharan.

Use the shared scheduling solver, Gantt/Calendar/Resource interfaces and separately validated Work Output and Materials calculators where units/source grades support them. Do not silently convert reference rates or unverified dimensions into approved work quantities, progress or procurement.

Preserve pilot and prior editions. Run source, scheduling, schema, privacy, kernel, and mobile/browser QA; update only public-safe projection and GitHub Actions/Pages after project approval for publication. Return live URLs, commit, run IDs, unresolved holds and an audit trail.

No structural or contractor approval is implied by successful GitHub Actions or published charts. A7 remains a pointer; the scheduling repository owns the engine and each project owns its input records.
